description: We are coders who love programming and solving strange problems.
summary: I wanted to share my love for space and what it takes to plan a space mission with others.
details:
ORBITAL is an educational space-mission design game. Players build a spacecraft, choose a launch service, check their design, and operate a mission while balancing cost, mass, power, communications, and science goals.

  • Earth missions: Configure an observation satellite, select an orbit, pass preflight checks, then schedule imaging and data transmission to map a simulated flood region.
  • Mars missions: Configure a rover and delivery system, complete a simulated landing, explore terrain, collect samples, and relay science back to Earth.
  • NASA data: Optional DONKI downloads provide space-weather reports for planning context. Imported NASA/JPL Horizons geometry supplies Earth–Mars distance and communication delay.
  • Interactive models: Players inspect spacecraft and planetary scenes. The rocket supports rotation, ignition, and exploded views.
  • Progress: Practice supports experimentation; Career tracks attempts and rewards improved results. Missions and their data provenance can be saved and exported.

The app runs locally in a browser. Platform launch scripts start a Python server, optionally retrieve NASA reports, and open the game. Standalone HTML supports offline play, although some model viewers still require internet.

Its physics and equipment values are simplified teaching models, rather than flight-qualified predictions.
